source: Moore S et al. 2018 - Dynamics of cholera epidemics from Benin to Mauritania (PLoS Negl Trop Dis 12(4):e0006379; Table 1 suspected cholera cases by country 2009-2015)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2010-01-01..2010-12-31. Source states: 'Following a three-year lull in the incidence of cholera, both Sierra Leone and Guinea experienced a trans-border epidemic in 2012, with 22,932 and 7,351 cases, respectively'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. National total (zero) - primary count; do not sum with sub-national rows. Table 1 ('The number of suspected cholera cases reported in each country included in the study per year') lists Sierra Leone explicitly with 0 suspected cases in 2009, 2010 and 2011 (2012: 23124; 2013: 377), and the authors state that 'the lack of cholera during a lull period is not due to inadequate surveillance or laboratory incompetence but simply due to the absence of cholera cases in the country' (field investigations in Sierra Leone with MoHS). Listed-with-0 + explicit lull statement = Documented_Absence (brief s.5). Corroboration: WHO 'Cholera, 2010' (WER 86(31), 29 Jul 2011) country table does not list Sierra Leone; its West Africa list is Benin 983, Cote d'Ivoire 32, Ghana 43, Liberia 1546, Senegal 3, Togo 72. Surveillance operational: weekly IDSR reporting was flowing (UN CERF RC/HC 2012: 'Through ongoing surveillance data reported weekly' D&V trends were tracked in 2011) and SLE detected and notified its 2008 (62 cases) and 2012 outbreaks. Regional picture: Guinea 0 in 2010 (42 in 2009, 3 in 2011 - quiet); Liberia 1546 suspected / 0 deaths in 2010 (Monrovia, endemic-level suspected reporting, no deaths 2010-2013); the 2010 West African epidemic was in the Lake Chad basin (Nigeria 44456, Chad 6395, Cameroon, Niger) and the wave reached Sierra Leone/Guinea only in 2012 (Moore et al.) - absence during a neighbour's low-level endemic reporting, not during a regional epidemic. Scope: the source spans 2009-2011, but 2009 (JHU UID 68) and 2011 (WHO UID 335, PHANTOM row) are baseline zero rows, so this row covers the effective gap 2010 only. CAUTION 2011 (Agent 6): UN CERF RC/HC 2012 says 'Cholera was suspected as early as November 2011' (D&V rise from 2 Nov 2011; first lab confirmation 16 Feb 2012), so the baseline's 2011 zero is doubtful for Nov-Dec 2011. Confidence 0.85 (Level 1; the table zero may partly reflect WHO annual non-listing). [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-10-02] QUALIFICATION (Agent 3, batch 8): 'operational' should be read as operational-but-weak - IDSR adopted in 2004 with 22 priority diseases by 2007, but WHO's Country Cooperation Strategy 2008-2013 (metadata 134) notes 'the challenge remains in scaling up the IDSR, low capacity for data management and analysis', and Njuguna et al. 2019 (metadata 125) call pre-2014 surveillance 'weak'. Weekly D&V tracking did operate (UN CERF 2012 for 2011) and Sierra Leone reported 1089 measles cases to WHO for 2010 (GHO). Confidence lowered 0.85 -> 0.8. (reason: Agent 3: surveillance-status qualification of own row 287) [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-10-02] Second independent peer-reviewed corroboration (Agent 3, batch 8): Blacklock et al. 2015, Global Health Action 8:25266 (PMC4286577): 'Prior to 2012, Sierra Leone had witnessed a series of smaller outbreaks, the most recent in 2008 with 62 reported cases' - i.e. no outbreak in 2009-2011. (reason: Agent 3: add second peer-reviewed corroboration to own row 287) [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-10-02] Nuance to the late-2011 caution (Agent 3, batch 9): WHO AFRO 'Health Topics (Sierra Leone)' (https://www.afro.who.int/countries/sierra-leone/topic/health-topics-sierra-leone): 'In November 2011, the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, through the weekly surveillance reporting system, noted an increase in the number of diarrhoea and vomiting cases. Samples revealed the causative organism as E. coli. In February 2012 ... Samples collected from Kambia, Port Loko and Pujehun confirmed Vibrio cholera 01 El-tor Ogawa.' So Nov-Dec 2011 was investigated and tested (E. coli), which supports the baseline 2011 zero, while UN CERF calls cholera 'suspected as early as November 2011' - Nov-Dec 2011 remains ambiguous (Agent 6).
